n2f110c4eedbb: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.
n3b77cbdb5e47: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.
nf703f9f76970: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.
n3f06131f0fe4: The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H 2 O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate 17,18 O-rich ices as the source of H 2 O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.
nafaaa0f402d4: Structural colors based on natural and artificial microstructures show promising light manipulation. As atomically thick building blocks, Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets have been successfully assembled into the ultrathin, flexible, arbitrarily cuttable, large-size structural colors by the simple and low-cost spray methods based on the lossy thin-film interference. By ordered stacking atomically thick Ti 3 C 2 T x layer by layer at well-organized low–surface tension semidry assemble state, rich colors from yellow to gray with the thickness from ∼22 to ∼154 nanometers of uniform Ti 3 C 2 T x colors are obtained, having the thinnest framework among solution-processed flexible structural colors with similar optical performance. Low-infrared emissivity from room to 300°C temperature and region-selective patterns make highly information-fused and complex visible-infrared (VIS-IR) Ti 3 C 2 T x colors camouflage. Without conventional dielectric layer between Ti 3 C 2 T x and substrate, automated spraying system can produce meter-scale films that can be cut and sewn into VIS-IR concealment “camouflage cloaks” easily, promising ultrathin multifunctional information systems and beyond.
nad5688a4efc0: Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8 + T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.
n8d466e262ba6: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. We find statistically significant negative trends across the Atlantic and Southern Oceans and positive trends in the Pacific Ocean. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.
ne70cdfb4fcb4: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.
nfe063d9825d7: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO x (NO and NO 2 ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.
n5c4fc2be4a6e: Tissue morphogenesis and postdevelopmental homeostasis rely on efficient information exchange between communicating cells. Cytonemes are actin-based protrusions that contribute to precise information flow by facilitating contact-mediated directional transport of diverse signaling cargoes. How pathway-specific cytonemes are formed is poorly understood, as are the molecular mechanisms promoting actin organization for elongation and stability of the dynamic cellular extensions. We investigated biogenesis of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) cytonemes, revealing functional repurposing of cell adhesion molecule-related proteins Brother of CDON (BOC) and Cell adhesion molecule-related, Down-regulated by Oncogenes (CDON) into recruiters of actin regulators FARP1 and Cdc42 for cytoneme elongation. Loss of BOC and CDON function blunts protrusion-localized Cdc42 activity, reducing cytoneme lengths and occurrence in SHH-expressing cells. Live imaging of developing murine spinal cords reveals that CDON loss in SHH-expressing cells reduces the frequency of neuroepithelial cytonemes and alters neuronal cell fate specification. These results inform a model whereby SHH-binding proteins promote ligand transport through stimulating formation of long cytonemes.
nce4649f44bcc: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.
n0d3bf5be2850: The fabrication of visible-spectrum three-dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) remains highly challenging, because existing manufacturing techniques cannot simultaneously achieve high processing precision and sufficient geometric freedom. Here, we propose a suspended pyrolysis-assisted two-photon polymerization (SP-TPP) printing strategy, achieving the controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D PhCs. The resulting 3D diamond PhCs exhibit a remarkable lattice-period standard deviation of only 5.75 nm, approximately 1/45 of that achieved without suspended pyrolysis. Microscopic reflection spectra confirm these PhCs possess uniform optical responses across all spatial positions. By tuning the lattice period and structural duty cycle, the PhCs operating at diverse wavelengths are systematically realized. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.
n99015ad78078: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.
n2cf6365e0c88: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.
n4d910e64681a: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser 273 , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.
nfd3727a659c3: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.
n9cc1a24a79be: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.
n35808e827900: Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the NAT1 motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the NAT1 motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of NAT1 -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.
n3058156fe0bb: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.
nb9d58e746029: Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. Using a forward genetic approach to generate loss of auditory function in zebrafish larvae, we identified a recessive mutation in split ends ( spen ), which encodes a transcription factor implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders in humans. We found that auditory sensorimotor deficits in spen mutants are associated with chronically elevated calcium levels in hindbrain radial astrocytes. Astrocytes have been previously implicated in the integration of neuronal inputs that alter arousal states and sensorimotor behavior. Inhibition of noradrenergic receptors, which are expressed in astrocytes, lowered calcium levels in mutant radial astrocytes and, notably, restored behavioral responses to sound in spen mutants. Our study highlights a role for noradrenergic signaling in spen -related disease and points to potential therapeutic approaches for pediatric patients.
n03ad782da733: The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca 2+ (Ca v 2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca v 2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.
n433aaac5ad14: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C 76 -linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from Amphidinium sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.
nb6a6167ce1a6: Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of CRYAB -linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.
n007489f94e08: It is highly desirable to design and engineer lightweight, low-power-consumption, and rapid physical intelligence (PI) structures that couple with multiple robotic functions. Here, we present a multimodal electromechanical switch (mEMS), consisting of a stretchable droplet-amplified electrostatic zipping structure, a convex bump, and a pair of electrical contacts, that can be used to achieve the widely used mechanical momentary, mechanical latching, and electrically actuated switching modes by simply tuning the applied voltage and using the same structure. We theoretically investigate the snap-through behavior of the elastic zipping membrane, which can be used to endow the mEMS with voltage-dependent memory, and the theoretical considerations are experimentally validated. As a result, we can apply the mEMS array for robotic memory, such as information writing and erasing; robotic communication by reprogrammable information encrypting, decrypting, and display; robotic computation by electrically reprogrammable logic gates; and reprogrammable binary information transferring. The mEMS represents a comprehensive PI structure for next-generation autonomous machines that can better adapt in unstructured and complex real-world environments.
n52b958360847: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.
na87656a1a8df: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)–component Schrödinger’s cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.
n412dabcb56ce: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.
nd9992fb1d6a7: Multicellular organisms produced by sexual reproduction develop from single cells, and the asymmetry of these cells can define the orientation of the earliest developmental axes. The haploid multicellular stage of the plant, Marchantia polymorpha, develops from a single cell—the spore—that divides asymmetrically, producing an apical germ cell that generates the plant body and a smaller basal cell that differentiates as an anchoring germ rhizoid cell. We show that the orientation of this asymmetric cell division is controlled by an external environmental cue—blue light—that is perceived by the photoreceptor phototropin. This process requires the NCH1 (NRL PROTEIN FOR CHLOROPLAST MOVEMENT 1) protein for downstream signaling. Together, these findings define core elements of the mechanism by which a directional environmental signal orients cell division, which, in turn, orients the first axis of symmetry.
n47b58fa1d275: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a radiation mechanism that circumvents this constraint by replacing the time-varying currents in conventional antennas with the mechanical twisting oscillation of a magnetic dipole. Using piezoelectrically actuated, biomimetic twisting resonators with ultrahigh mechanical quality factors, we demonstrate that low-frequency antennas operating at 15.4 and 668 hertz can be miniaturized to centimeter- and millimeter-scale, respectively, with radiation efficiencies exceeding those of size-matched loop antennas by factors of 49,000 and 5000, respectively. This electromechanical-magnetic transduction enables underwater cross-medium communication over 115 meters with only milliwatt-level power consumption, using 99.9% less power than loop antennas. It also supports implantable wireless devices that achieve a fourfold increase in communication range at identical power consumption, opening a route to long-range, low-power wireless systems capable of operating in some of the most demanding environments.
nabc16f11c746: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.
n1fe1e7aae435: Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H 2 O 2 generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH 3 ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.
n172fdd673de7: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that drives macrophage functions ranging from tissue homeostasis to inflammation, yet how STAT3 specifies these divergent outcomes remains unclear. By integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with selective STAT3 degradation, we show that STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages. Graded STAT3 chromatin recruitment scales with locus-specific H3K27ac deposition and transcriptional output across homeostatic and inflammatory programs. STAT3 degradation permits STAT1 recruitment at a subset of regulatory regions and engages a delayed amplification loop that is partially dependent on STING and type I IFN signaling. In severe COVID-19, monocytes exhibit exaggerated STAT3-associated inflammatory signatures together with attenuated STAT1-associated interferon responses, consistent with a skewed STAT3-STAT1 balance. These findings define a framework in which STAT3 calibrates IL-6–induced chromatin output while maintaining pathway fidelity by limiting STAT1 cross-talk.
n24a1e29126b3: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.
nd0618df59e96: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell–derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.
nde948c20b9fa: The basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the M. viride PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C 2 S 2 M p2 L p2 -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll b macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.
ncc14cfee38c8: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.
n0bae7c270717: The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of SPL29 for reproductive transition, BA1 for female inflorescence initiation, and EXPA5 for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of ZmMYC2a/b or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.
n037234caea3f: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Using MRIs from 2187 participants, alongside normative data, we systematically investigated network-based mechanisms underlying MS-related atrophy. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.
n5b1b1c1ae2ad: Rice roots have a distinctive ground tissue architecture with multiple cortical layers and a single endodermal layer concentrically surrounding the stele. This architecture promotes aerenchyma formation and adaptability to waterlogged environments, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified the INDETERMINATE DOMAIN (IDD) and SHORTROOT (SHR) families as key regulators of ground tissue development in rice. OsIDD2/3/6/8 govern cortical radial symmetry by coordinating cortical organization and auxin distribution independently of OsSHR1/2/3/4/5. Quadruple knockout of OsIDD2/3/6/8 caused cortical asymmetry without affecting apoplastic barrier integrity or mineral uptake but reduced shoot-directed ion transport. OsIDD8 also controls the number of cortical cell layers and endodermal cells, whereas OsSHR1/2/3/4/5 redundantly promote periclinal divisions of the cortical cells, which require OsIDD8 activity. Moreover, OsIDD and OsSHR members coordinate endodermal differentiation by regulating localization of Casparian strip membrane domain protein OsCASP1 and lignin/suberin deposition. These findings establish a genetic framework underlying the spatial organization and functional differentiation of ground tissue in rice roots.
n93639eb99bc7: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We investigate the population dynamics underlying the emergence and persistence of this gradient through two successive human range expansions. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.
ne79b1943600b: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.
neb35e01c3464: Fully automated cranes are revolutionizing modern port operations by addressing labor shortages, improving precision, and enhancing safety. Toward this goal, we present the Autane (autonomous crane) system specifically developed for rubber tire gantry (RTG) cranes handling standardized containers in port yards, enabling autonomous safety-critical container grabbing, transport, and placement with high accuracy, adaptability, and efficiency. Autane overcomes the challenges of safe motion of large-scale cranes with centimeter-level precision requirements, providing long-distance high-precision perception. It uses multisensor fusion, real-time obstacle detection, and simultaneous localization and mapping to perceive the environment, identify container features, and dynamically adjust trajectories. By tightly coupling perception, planning, control, and operation and maintenance, Autane achieves safe and precise alignment, seamless interaction with transport vehicles, and robust execution of long-distance handling tasks. Deployed in multiple ports, Autane shows full-day operation and has autonomously handled more than 2 million 20-foot equivalent units. This work highlights the potential of fully autonomous RTG cranes to enable sustained, resilient, and low-intervention port automation.
nfc826fbc9d95: Automation of heavy machinery offers the opportunity to improve productivity in mechanized industries such as construction, mining, and material handling. Yet, automation of such machines is challenged by their complex dynamics, in part because of hydraulic actuation that involves fluids, flexible elements, and nonlinear delays. A concomitant challenge is the size and weight of these machines, which can make experiments on the physical systems exceedingly dangerous. Here, we show that reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation, followed by transfer of the learned policies from simulation to reality, can successfully automate acrobatic maneuvers that push a heavy construction machine to the limits of its actuation and have only previously been accomplished by a small number of elite human operators in official world-record performances. We trained policies that perform autonomous acrobatic maneuvers on a John Deere 332G, an operational 5-tonne skid-steer loader. The policies can autonomously swing the machine up onto two wheels and, while balancing on two wheels, drive over rough terrain, trace out specified trajectories, spin around, and swing the bucket back and forth before landing it safely back onto four wheels. This work demonstrates that RL and sim-to-real transfer enable dynamic autonomous control of heavy machinery, directly contributing to greater automation in heavy equipment sectors.
n44068114d360: Robot acceptance is shaped by dynamic, multimodal interactions that influence trust, comfort, and behavioral intentions.
n331aff35cb49: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy for which neoadjuvant chemotherapy with albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with gemcitabine (AG) is a standard first-line approach for borderline resectable and locally advanced disease. However, secondary resistance to this regimen is common, and its underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. In this study, we investigated how neoadjuvant AG therapy shapes the tumor stroma in PDAC. Single-cell transcriptomics of patient tumors revealed that AG treatment induces a phenotypic switch of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) from myofibroblastic (myCAF) to inflammatory (iCAF) states and identified a previously unrecognized TMEM100 + CAF subset enriched in nonresponders. Mechanistic studies showed that albumin-bound paclitaxel activates IL-2–STAT5 signaling to drive TMEM100 expression and that TMEM100 + CAFs promote chemoresistance through paracrine secretion of amphiregulin (AREG) and activation of tumor EGFR signaling. Genetic ablation of TMEM100 + CAFs in mouse models reversed CAF switching and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of AG therapy. These findings map chemotherapy-induced CAF plasticity, reveal a TMEM100-AREG axis of resistance, and highlight TMEM100 + CAFs as a promising target to sensitize PDAC to neoadjuvant treatment.
n92cbae613d98: Osteoarthritis (OA), a leading cause of disability, is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic dysregulation in chondrocytes. TNF-α and IL-1β are key inflammatory drivers in OA pathogenesis, but clinical trials targeting them individually have been unsuccessful, highlighting the potential need for dual-targeting strategies. By screening a US Food and Drug Administration–approved drug library, we identified dabigatran, a thrombin inhibitor, as a potent dual suppressor of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling that restored chondrocyte metabolism. In preclinical OA models, including both mice and cynomolgus macaques, dabigatran attenuated cartilage degeneration, alleviated pain, and improved joint function. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms, we performed biochemical copurification coupled with mass spectrometry, identifying brefeldin A–inhibited guanine nucleotide–exchange protein 2 (BIG2) as a previously unknown dabigatran-binding target. Mechanistically, dabigatran binds to BIG2, promoting BIG2-dependent TNFR1 release to dampen TNF-α signaling while enhancing BIG2-mediated IL-1R1 degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway to limit IL-1β effects. These findings establish BIG2-mediated receptor trafficking and membrane dynamics as a regulatory node that concurrently inhibits TNF-α and IL-1β signaling, suggesting this pathway as a potential therapeutic strategy for OA.
n8aeb35e8ddd6: Pharmacogenomics promises improved outcomes through individualized prescribing. However, the lack of diversity in pharmacogenomics studies impedes clinical translation and the application of precision medicine across populations. We evaluated the frequencies of variants in 16 pharmacogenes ( ABCG2 , CACNA1S , CYP2D6 , CYP2C Cluster , CYP2C19 , CYP2C9 , CYP3A5 , CYP4F2 , DPYD , G6PD , NUDT15 , RYR1 , SLCO1B1 , TPMT , UGT1A1 , and VKORC1 ) and predicted phenotypes and medication exposures using whole-genome sequencing and electronic health record data from nearly 100,000 All of Us Research Program participants. We report that 100% of participants carried at least one pharmacogenomic variant and nearly all (99.5%) had a predicted phenotype with prescribing recommendations. Clinical impact was high with 24.4% of participants having both an actionable phenotype for these pharmacogenes and a prior exposure to an impacted medication with pharmacogenomic prescribing guidance. Importantly, we report thousands of previously unrecognized pharmacogene variants and hundreds of alleles and predicted phenotypes that deviate from known frequencies across populations or were previously unreported, especially in the Americas and African ancestry groups.
n55af5e608ade: Human infections with mpox virus (MPXV) since 2022 have resulted in more than 188,000 cases reported globally as of June 2026, highlighting the urgent need for effective therapeutics. Here, we recruited smallpox vaccinees and donors with incidental vaccinia virus (VACV) exposure and isolated a panel of human anti-A33/A35 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from the latter using recombinant MPXV A35 as a cross-reactive bait. These mAbs recognized four distinct nonoverlapping epitopes (epitopes 1 to 4) and one composite epitope (epitope 3 + 4) on MPXV A35 and exhibited cross-reactivity against multiple orthopoxviruses (OPXVs). Cryo–electron microscopy structural analysis revealed that the high-affinity epitope 3 + 4 mAb HD15 engages an epitope at the A35 dimer interface that is conserved across OPXVs. Combinations of mAbs targeting nonoverlapping epitopes mediated synergistic, Fc-dependent neutralization in vitro; conferred therapeutic protection against lethal VACV challenge; and reduced viral burden and disease severity after MPXV challenge in mice. Together, these findings establish a single-antigen, multiepitope strategy for the development of broadly protective therapeutics against OPXVs.
n85a521a02964: Although EGFR inhibitors are highly effective for treating EGFR- mutant lung adenocarcinomas ( EGFR + LUADs), resistance inevitably emerges, with histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) representing a particularly aggressive mechanism. Our prospective trial enrolled patients with EGFR + LUAD at high risk of transformation ( TP53 / RB1 -deficient) and treated them with first-line osimertinib combined with platinum and etoposide. Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months. Genomic and single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patient samples revealed clinical and subclinical plasticity associated with TP53 / RB1 comutations, including histological transformation to SCLC, as well as mesenchymal and squamous histologies. These changes in plasticity were linked to progressive disruption of the RB pathway, leading to altered chromatin accessibility and induction of neuronal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition transcriptional programs, further intensified by osimertinib treatment. These findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.
n9caae3a8a2b7: Slow waves during sleep are fundamental for neural homeostasis, metabolic regulation, and waste clearance and are known to be altered in neurodegenerative diseases. Sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) have been observed in awake, healthy individuals, where they are linked to fluctuations in vigilance and mind-wandering. Whether SLSWs are altered in Parkinson’s disease (PD), and whether such alterations contribute to psychiatric or cognitive complications, remains unknown. In a cohort of 84 nondemented patients with PD and 30 healthy older adults, we found that SLSWs occurred more frequently in patients with PD. Hallucinatory traits in patients with PD were associated with higher SLSW amplitude, especially over frontocentral regions. Moreover, more prominent SLSWs were associated with poorer cognitive functions. We conclude that, whereas slow waves during sleep have positive physiological functions, exacerbated diurnal SLSWs may reflect responses related to PD neuropathology, at the cost of hallucinations and reduced cognitive function.
n3d4f913838e9: Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO x /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we designed a low-power edge detection unit using dual random number hardware computation. Its energy consumption is 92.3% lower than traditional logic circuits, with strong anti-interference. To validate practical use, we constructed a 32-channel parallel full-hardware system with 64 devices, achieving 31.25 frames per second and excellent edge detection. The system exhibits excellent scalability, stability, and anti-interference, offering great potential for edge vision hardware in autonomous driving, safety monitoring, and surgical assistance.
n77d419b60d20: Polyradicals in open-shell polycyclic hydrocarbons (PHs) offer access to multiple spin states and hold great promise for spintronics and quantum technologies. Here we report a nonalternant, air-stable tetraradical featuring two fused 7-5-7 rings and a strongly correlated singlet ground state. This molecule displays an exceptional tetraradical character ( y 0 = 1.00, y 1 = 0.89) and exhibits long ambient stability ( t 1/2 = 33 days). Comprehensive electronic structure and magnetic response analyses reveal that the spin topology is governed by both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, with robust electron correlation ( J 1 = +321 K, J 2 = −44 K, and J 3 = −29 K). The unique nonalternant design suppresses hyperfine and vibrational decoherence, giving rise to long spin relaxation and coherence time. These findings demonstrate that embedding nonalternant motifs into PH polyradicals provides a powerful strategy to simultaneously promote molecular stability, spin-exchange coupling, and spin robustness—key features for materials in the rising field of quantum information science.
ne96b6a380591: Andes virus (ANDV) causes hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), with rare outbreaks involving person-to-person transmission. A human ANDV isolate from one such outbreak and a rodent isolate from the same region differ in lethality in Syrian golden hamsters. Genomic analysis revealed 25 nonsynonymous substitutions, including one leading to a T641I change in the human ANDV glycoprotein precursor near its cleavage site. Although the isolates differed in growth kinetics, strand-specific RT-qPCR did not support major differences in viral RNA synthesis, whereas virion release was delayed in the case of the human isolate. In human cell expression systems, a single I641T substitution in the human ANDV glycoprotein resulted in decreased Golgi retention and faster release of virion-like particles relative to wild-type glycoprotein. Since ANDV egress takes place at the Golgi, the T641I change present in the human ANDV isolate may represent a human adaptive mutation influencing glycoprotein trafficking and virus particle release.
n3342242940d2: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing ( n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions ( n = 42), and histology ( n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2 + cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition–like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.
nc26344de0b0b: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated “locomotion-perception-action” workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.
n5a6e9b641607: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.
n5f87cdbccbc3: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin ( Penk ), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)–mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. These findings propose a central mechanism underlying cold-induced pain relief, which could be a novel therapeutic target.
n98800bd1bc5a: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8 + T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)–regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8 + T cell–dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8 + T cell–mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8 + T cell–induced endothelial death in CM.
ne780a68d0e39: Aeromonas , widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol’s antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5′-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. In the sturgeon infection model, resveratrol-nanoemulsion notably improved survival, reduced tissue bacterial loads, mitigated oxidative stress and inflammation, and restored intestinal barrier function. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii , with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.
nb8120c847d2c: Bystander T cells eradicate tumors in the absence of antigen recognition.
ne8addbc9c6d0: Aberrant, cranial bone marrow–derived myelopoiesis drives neuroinflammation in chronic traumatic brain injury.
nb1a0b20d2f0b: In vivo cell engineering enables the direct programming of immune cells inside patients. Instead of isolating, modifying, and reinfusing cells, therapeutic instructions are delivered directly to selected immune cells through lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors. This approach could facilitate rapid and scalable deployment of varied immune cell therapies across disease contexts. Early clinical studies in oncology and autoimmunity demonstrate increasing technical and clinical feasibility. The next challenge lies in enhancing precision to ensure that vectors reach the target cell type and tissue, deliver the appropriate payload, and produce desired transient or durable activity. Progress in targeting ligands, vector design, biodistribution control, and genome editing is beginning to address these barriers. Ensuring safety against immunogenicity, inflammatory toxicity, off-target editing, and uncontrolled persistence remains a central priority. By mastering these constraints, in vivo engineering could turn endogenous immune cells into therapeutic agents generated directly in the body, expanding cell therapy to diseases refractory to current modalities.
n902d8d278f8c: The interleukin-36 receptor (IL-36R) drives proinflammatory signaling and is therapeutically targeted by spesolimab in acute skin inflammation. Beyond its three canonical agonists (IL-36α, IL-36β, and IL-36γ), IL-36R was recently proposed to be activated by IL-37. Together with antagonism by IL-36R antagonist (IL-36RA) and IL-38, this creates a complex structure-function landscape that remains poorly understood. Here, we report the cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of human IL-36γ bound to IL-36R and the shared co-receptor IL-1R accessory protein (IL-1RAcP). IL-36γ engages IL-36R with low affinity, enabling high-affinity IL-1RAcP recruitment. IL-37 exhibits the opposite binding signature, binding IL-36R with high affinity but IL-1RAcP weakly. Functional comparison of IL-36R engagement by IL-36γ and IL-37 confirmed their common proinflammatory signature, with IL-36γ exhibiting markedly higher potency, consistent with its more stable signaling complex. Structural comparison of cytokine-bound versus antibody-antagonized IL-36R revealed that spesolimab acts as an allosteric antagonist. This study therefore provides a structural and mechanistic blueprint for IL-36R activation by distinct cytokines.
n87060a719042: New tools feed humanity’s ancient impulse to embellish and self-aggrandize, but future scholars will be prepared
n7ad77a0a327b: The result, one of three major claims from OpenAI, raises questions about sharing of AI-generated work
ndb8134de2770: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.
